# DropSpace v0.3.0-preview.19 — Architecture remediation

<!-- update-summary: Preview.19 adds atomic batch pinning, explicit peer trust lifecycle, lossless cleanup and revoke recovery, immutable share staging, cancellation-safe shutdown ownership, locked dependencies, x64-only declarations, and owner-authorized create-once release publication. -->

Preview.19 is the architecture-remediation release following the Preview.18 audit. It preserves the Windows 10 version 1809 / Build 17763 and later x64 boundary, local-first storage, external-file safety rule, existing Overlay and Clipboard product paths, and Stable/Preview update-channel contract.

## Reliability and data safety

- Pin and unpin batches are owned by an application use case and one SQLite transaction. Undo records only the rows that actually changed, so missing, pending-delete, duplicate, and already-correct rows are not silently rewritten.
- Clipboard, DropLink, Nearby, DNS-SD, and file-metadata shutdown paths distinguish cancellation from timeout. Worker-owned gates, cancellation sources, sockets, finalizers, and staging directories remain owned until their work reaches a terminal state.
- App-owned payload-delete obligations use lossless segmented journals that survive large backlogs, malformed/partial entries, restart, duplicate entries, and compaction interruption. External source paths remain reference-only.
- Nearby and encrypted Internet Share creation prune expired entries before admission, enforce a hard live-share cap without evicting live capabilities, and reserve revoke-handle capacity before contacting the backend.
- Secure Internet Share sources are copied once into an app-owned immutable staging snapshot, hash/length checked, and uploaded only from that snapshot.
- Update-state recovery parses all bounded cache entries before selecting the highest valid version. Temporary private-key/PFX buffers are cleared, and dropped-log counts remain available through an emergency shutdown diagnostic.

## Device trust and compatibility

- Pairing now persists `PairingPending`, `Trusted`, `UnpairPending`, and `Blocked`. Restart reconciliation requires both a usable DPAPI secret and `Trusted` state before DropLink authentication is accepted.
- MainPage event subscriptions are reload-safe, legacy overlay placement fields have a concrete post-Preview.19 retirement condition, and public/build declarations are unambiguously x64-only until an ARM64 evidence track exists.
- Credential-like environment/key files are ignored and tracked-tree hygiene is checked in CI and release workflows.

## Release and verification

- NuGet restore uses committed lock files and locked mode. The release lane uses the named `windows-2025` runner and publishes a build-environment record containing runner, .NET, SDK, MSBuild, Windows SDK, Inno Setup, and signing metadata.
- Pushes and pull requests validate only. Publication is owner-authorized, main-only, create-once, and refuses an existing tag or release; Stable publication remains signing-gated.
- The five public assets are `DropSpace-x64.msix`, `DropSpace.exe`, `DropSpaceSetup.exe`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and `update-manifest.json`.

Preview publication may remain unsigned. SmartScreen may show an unknown-publisher warning; download only from the official [GitHub Release](https://github.com/airanluo-dot/DropSpace/releases) and compare `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

Hosted Windows CI/release and website/browser-route checks are the automated gates. Real Windows OS/DPI/OLE/accessibility, two-device transfer, deployed Worker/browser, and performance evidence remain explicitly conditional until recorded on their target environments.
